NOSTRADAMUS - Open Call #1: Funding Digital Applications for Sustainable and Efficient Agriculture
item.description:
NOSTRADAMUS Open Call #1 invites system actors and innovators (SMEs, start-ups, small mid-caps, RTOs, end-user organisations) to design, develop, test, and validate multi-functional, open-source digital applications for farm decision-making and agribusiness.

Selected Third Parties will build upon the NOSTRADAMUS data infrastructure - including multi-dimensional Open Data Cubes, Analysis Ready Data (ARD) Earth Observation pipelines, real-time IoT Observatory streams, and socio-economic datasets - to deliver data-driven tools that optimize agricultural inputs (water, fertilizers, pesticides), improve energy balance, and enhance production resilience in cereal-based agricultural systems.

The call covers 5 designated topics:

  1. Topic 1 (T1): Sustainable crop production and optimisation of cereal-based systems under changing climate and soil conditions.
  2. Topic 2 (T2): Nutrient and soil health management, integrating soil fertility indicators, organic matter dynamics, and precision fertilisation models.  
  3. Topic 3 (T3): Water resource efficiency and drought resilience, using Early Warning System outputs and IoT-based soil moisture monitoring.  
  4. Topic 4 (T4): Smart and predictive pest and disease management to support the EU objective of reducing pesticide dependency.  
  5. Topic 5 (T5): Open topic (integrated, cross-domain decision-support applications combining at least two topics T1–T4).  

Awarded Third Parties must participate in a 12-month 4-Sprint program (Training, Design, Development & Validation, Demonstration & Assessment), physically demonstrate their application at 1 primary NOSTRADAMUS pilot site (DE, RS, CH, SI, or CY), deliver at least 1 user training session, release their source code as open-source, and author an EIP-AGRI Practice Abstract.

item.title: Mission ocean in Slovenian seas — Call for proposals for the provision of financial support to third parties for the implementation of small-scale projects under the RISTANC project
item.description:
1. Purpose of the call

The call is published as part of the implementation of the European RISTANC project, which is financed by the Horizon Europe programme. The project contributes to the implementation of the EU Mission “Restore Our Ocean and Waters by 2030”, with a focus on the Slovenian marine area, which is prt of the cross-border North Adriatic region.

2. Key challenges

The call encourages projects that contribute to addressing the following thematic areas:

  1. The establishment and management of moorings in the Slovenian sea for recreational and tourist vessels that prevent damage to marine seabed habitats,
  2. The planning and implementation of interventions in the coastal zone of the Slovenian sea that harmonise the various needs and interests of people and the environment,
  3. Other measures in the Slovenian sea area (and potentially beyond) that contribute to the objectives of the EU Mission “Restore Our Ocean & Waters”, such as reducing pollution in the marine environment (including plastic and other waste), the conservation and restoration of marine ecosystems, and the development of a sustainable blue economy.

3. Eligible activities

Activities eligible under the call are those that contribute to the objectives of the RISTANC project and the EU Mission “Restore Our Ocean & Waters”, and address one or more of the challenges listed inthe call. The following types of activities, in particular, are eligible:

  1. Experimental activities (projects implementing innovative approaches in support of the Mission “Restore Our Ocean & Waters”, i.e. for the cleaning, protection, or restoration of the marine environment, or for the establishment of a zero-emission, circular, and sustainable blue economy).
  2. Prototype development (activities focused on developing prototypes to solve specific challenges related to marine ecosystems).
  3. Feasibility studies and scoping (assessing the feasibility of larger-scale measures).
  4. Research and innovation (initiatives to research new methods or technologies that contribute to reducing pollution and to the protection or restoration of biodiversity, including improvements to regulatory frameworks and governance structures).
  5. Artistic, cultural and community activities (initiatives and programmes that use art and culture to engage local communities in pollution prevention, nature protection and restoration, and awareness campaigns on ocean health and related human well-being).
  6. Educational activities and capacity-building initiatives (education, training and workshops for stakeholders, children, young people and adults, including professionals, to strengthen knowledge, competencies and skills in sustainable practices related to reducing pollution, the conservation or restoration of biodiversity, and the sustainable blue economy).
  7. Monitoring and citizen science activities (activities to assess the effectiveness and impacts of implemented solutions on marine ecosystems, citizen science activities).
  8. Knowledge brokering and transfer (activities that translate existing research results into actionable evidence for policy-making or practice, such as synthesis reports, policy recommendations, stakeholder dialogues, living labs, etc.; also includes institutions as focal points for transdisciplinary research and innovation activities with European reach).
  9. A combination of the above activities.

Proposed projects must contribute to the development of sustainable and inclusive solutions for challenges facing the marine environment in the North Adriatic area.

4. Duration

The project shall commence on the date the funding agreement is signed (no earlier than 1.1.2027) and may last for a minimum of 6 and a maximum of 12 months. Regardless of the project duration, it must be completed by 28 February 2028 at the latest.

item.title: LLM-BRIDGE – Venture Incubation Programme - Open Call for Incubators – 2nd Call
item.description:
The Venture Incubation Programme (VIP) serves as an instrument to strengthening incubation capacity in Europe to support early-stage GenAI ventures as well as to:

  1. Accelerate the commercialisation of LLM technologies, providing mentoring, access to high-performance computing (HPC) resources, data infrastructures, and regulatory guidance.
  2. Promote responsible AI innovation, aligned with the AI Act, Data Act, GDPR, and the EU’s Digital Decade Targets.
  3. Foster cross-border collaboration, knowledge sharing, and participation of underrepresented regions and groups in the European AI ecosystem.


Through this call, LLM-BRIDGE seeks to identify and support one high-quality, EU-based incubator capable of supporting startups in the transforming of early-stage GenAI ideas into viable, scalable, and ethically compliant ventures that may be eligible to apply for the future Long Jump and European Grand Challenges. Participating in the VIP provides an opportunity for a leading incubator to position itself at the forefront of Europe’s generative AI revolution. This collaboration offers strategic, reputational, and operational advantages, aligning the incubator with a pan-European initiative that seeks to redefine the future of AI-driven innovation and technological leadership. 

The VIP programme will select one incubator to run a 12-week VIP cohort across Europe, which will:

  1. Deliver structured training and mentoring to 30 startups.
  2. Provide and facilitate access to technical expertise and AI infrastructures.
  3. Monitor and report progress using standardised KPIs defined in the Annex I. 
  4. Contribute to the overall impact of LLM-BRIDGE and the European GenAI innovation ecosystem.

The selected incubator will gain direct access to a carefully selected pipeline of high-potential GenAI startups from across Europe, allowing it to deepen its expertise in nurturing deep-tech ventures with the potential to drive the next wave of generative AI solutions. Such engagement not only enhances the incubators reputation as a leading enabler of cutting-edge innovation but also strengthens its market position within the highly competitive AI ecosystem.

item.title: ForestPathways – Building Knowledge and Solutions for Resilient Forests and Sustainable Forest-Based Futures
item.description:
The FOREST Joint Call 2026 – ForestPathways supports transnational research and innovation activities across the spectrum from fundamental research to applied research and, where appropriate, demonstration activities. Projects are expected to generate new knowledge, develop practical solutions, and contribute to implementation in policy, management or industry contexts, while considering the diversity of forests and the forest-based sector.

Applicants must select the single topic that best reflects the primary focus of their proposal. Proposals may address multiple topics but will be evaluated and ranked under one primary topic.

TOPIC 1 – Climate-Resilient Forest Systems: “How forests function and respond to climate change”

This topic supports research and innovation addressing the resilience, adaptive capacity, and long-term sustainability of forest ecosystems under changing environmental conditions, including climate change and increasing disturbance pressures. It aims to strengthen the scientific basis for climate-resilient forest systems and support their adaptation and mitigation to climate change, within broader environmental and socioeconomic contexts.

Proposals should address, where relevant, carbon dynamics measurement, monitoring and assessment of carbon stocks and sinks; adaptation pathways and strategies; forest ecosystem processes and dynamics; disturbance regimes, including wildfires and other abiotic and biotic disturbances, pests and diseases; landscape-level interactions and spatial dynamics; and genetic diversity and adaptive capacity, including assisted migration.

TOPIC 2 – Adaptive and Multifunctional Forest Management Systems: “How forests should be managed under changing conditions”

This topic supports research and innovation focused on the implementation of adaptive and multifunctional forest management systems that enhance resilience, sustainability, and the provision of multiple ecosystem services. It aims to support forest management approaches capable of responding to ecological change, disturbance risks, and evolving environmental, economic, and societal demands.

Proposals should address, where relevant, silvicultural systems and management approaches supporting resilient and multifunctional forests; sustainable harvesting and wood mobilisation methods; monitoring, assessment and planning tools for adaptive management; integration of forest genetic resources into management strategies; operational, digital and technical innovations; risk reduction and adaptation strategies; and trade-offs and synergies between ecosystem services.

TOPIC 3 – Timber and Innovative Wood-Based Products: “How wood is transformed into innovative products”

This topic supports research and innovation on the development, performance, and uptake of timber and innovative wood-based products contributing to decarbonisation and the circular bioeconomy. It aims to advance the development and market uptake of sustainable wood-based products and systems, supporting the substitution of fossil-based and carbon-intensive materials and contributing to low-carbon construction and manufacturing.

Proposals should address, where relevant, engineered timber and timber construction systems; high-value wood-based products, chemicals and materials; substitution of fossil-based and other carbon-intensive materials; more sustainable alternatives to polluting wood treatments and processing practices; standardisation, testing and certification; circular and resource-efficient use of wood-based products; innovative use of underutilised softwood and hardwood species; innovative manufacturing technologies; and approaches to increase market demand and consumer acceptance and uptake.

TOPIC 4 – Forest Value Chains, Markets and Governance: “How forest-based sectors, markets and governance are organised”

This topic supports research and innovation strengthening the resilience, sustainability, and functioning of forest-based value chains, markets, and governance systems, supporting the transition towards a sustainable and circular forest-based bioeconomy. It aims to support resilient, sustainable, competitive, and innovative forest-based value chains and governance systems capable of responding to environmental, economic, and societal transitions.

Proposals should address, where relevant, forest-based value chains and market organisation; innovative business models, economic viability and investment readiness; policy, regulatory and governance instruments; barriers to market uptake and innovation deployment; cascading use, circularity and efficient resource use; skills, labour, education and workforce development; and European resilience in sustainable raw material supply, value chains, local processing capacities and forest-based economies.

The topics provide strategic direction and facilitate evaluation. They are not exhaustive and do not restrict the submission of innovative or cross-cutting proposals aligned with the overall objectives of the call.

item.description:
Basic information

AENAON implements two competitive Open Call rounds through its Financial Support to Third Parties (FSTP) scheme. The Open Calls aim to maximise the uptake, integration, testing and validation of AENAON technologies and services, including the Federated Digital Twin-based Cyber Range Platform, cybersecurity training capabilities and cybersecurity preparedness services, in realistic offshore wind and related critical-infrastructure environments.

The Open Calls are designed to engage SMEs and start-ups, large enterprises and technology providers, research organisations and universities, cybersecurity service and technology providers, offshore wind operators, manufacturers and supply-chain actors, energy and critical-infrastructure stakeholders, and other relevant innovation actors. Supported third-party projects are expected to contribute practical use cases, validation evidence, technical feedback and sector-relevant results that strengthen the cybersecurity and resilience of the offshore wind ecosystem.

Open Call 1 focuses on the initial validation, integration and testing of AENAON technologies and services in realistic environments. Activities may include the development and validation of sector-specific cybersecurity scenarios, identification and assessment of offshore-wind-relevant vulnerabilities, integration with simulation and cyber range environments, cybersecurity testing and training activities, and validation of cybersecurity tools, services and preparedness capabilities.

Open Call 1 sub-projects are expected to have an implementation period of 8 months, with clearly defined tasks, milestones, deliverables, KPIs and acceptance evidence.

Applicants may propose activities related to cybersecurity testing and validation, cyber range training and scenario-based exercises, vulnerability assessment, penetration testing, threat and risk assessment, risk monitoring, cyberattack management, digital twin-based validation and integration, or other cybersecurity resilience use cases that are demonstrably aligned with the objectives and technical capabilities of AENAON.

Budget

The total AENAON FSTP budget is €4,100,000.

The indicative allocation is:

  1. €2,100,000 for Open Call 1
  2. €2,000,000 for Open Call 2

Any amount not committed under Open Call 1 may be reallocated to Open Call 2, subject to budget availability, the applicable Open Call rules and the principles of transparency, equal treatment and sound financial management.

Funding Constraints

AENAON will provide sub-grants under two Open Calls (Open Call 1 and 2), with a total FSTP allocation of €4,100,000. In line with the call topic, the scheme derogates from the €60k ceiling, allowing up to €100,000 per individual third party (only in the case of offshore wind farm operators and manufacturers, which are considered large critical infrastructures/ operators of essential services) and up to €150,000 per action (in case of small consortia).

Example 1 — SME A, Open Call 1

  1. Entity A is a generic SME, applicable ceiling: €60,000
  2. Funding requested/awarded in Open Call 1: €55,000
  3. Result: Eligible (Remaining funding capacity for Open Call 2 under AENAON: €5,000, if applicable)

Example 2 — Offshore wind-farm operator B, Open Call 1

  1. Entity B is an offshore wind-farm operator and therefore benefits from the derogated ceiling; applicable ceiling: €100,000
  2. Funding awarded in Open Call 1: €87,000
  3. Result: Eligible (Remaining funding capacity for Open Call 2: €13,000, if applicable)

Example 3 — Small consortium B + C, Open Call 2

  1. In Open Call 2, B and C form a small consortium. B = offshore wind-farm operator/manufacturer, and C = SME, thus, maximum funding per consortium action: €150,000.
  2. However, the individual ceilings must also be respected. Since B already received €87,000 in Open Call 1, B can receive only €100,000 − €87,000 = €13,000
  3. C has received no previous AENAON funding. Therefore, C can receive up to €60,000
  4. The total maximum eligible AENAON funding for the consortium (B+C) in Open Call 2 is therefore €73,000 (B up to €13,000, C up to €60,000)
  5. Consortium action (budget requested): €73k < €150k maximum per action

The final lump-sum amount awarded to each selected third-party beneficiary will be fixed at the contracting stage through a needs-based, auditable right-sizing process, taking into account the proposed activities, technical complexity, budget needs, expected contribution to AENAON objectives, evaluation outcome, milestones, deliverables, and acceptance criteria.

Payment Schedule

AENAON applies a staged payment model of 30% – 40% – 30%:

  1. 30% initial payment upon signature of the Sub-Grant Agreement and completion of onboarding requirements
  2. 40% interim payment following successful completion of the mid-term review and acceptance of required interim reports, deliverables and supporting evidence
  3. 30% final payment following completion of the action and acceptance of the final report, final deliverables, performance evidence and required outputs

Payments are conditional upon the satisfactory achievement of agreed milestones, deliverables and acceptance criteria. Payments may be suspended, reduced or recovered in cases of non-performance, breach of contractual obligations, false declarations, conflict of interest, ineligible activities or serious non-compliance with reporting, ethics, GDPR, visibility or audit requirements.

CodeSupply aggregates and curates comprehensive software metadata, including origin and licensing information, security vulnerabilities, and quality metrics from distributed, authoritative data sources across programming ecosystems and software types. This metadata is assembled in reference data sets, federated in a unified data catalog for digital sovereignty and independence, and distributed as open data, freely available to all, using an open source data license.


The CodeSupply project pursues three interconnected objectives that directly address data challenges in cybersecurity, software supply chain management, and regulatory and open source license compliance:

  1. Publish current, correct, and comprehensive software metadata
  2. Establish a scalable and sustainable mechanism to provide democratic access to data sets
  3. Create a foundational framework for future iterations, enhancements, and new data sets


CodeSupply will deliver an ambitious development effort, but this is a vast domain with many more challenges than what any preconceived effort could tackle by itself. This is why we invite your contribution to help us reshape the state of play, and together create an open, trustworthy and reliable internet for all.

ECT2 will expand the existing portfolio of whole-city transformation activities and interventions by focusing on implementation barriers shared by cities across the Mission.

The core shift introduced in this call is a move away from broad, domain-based support towards a more focused model that organises action around clearly defined systemic barriers and bottlenecks.

To this end, ECT2 is organised around six challenge areas which represent critical city-wide implementation barriers that currently prevent cities from translating Climate City Contract ambitions into replicable and scalable outcomes.

The challenge areas are:

  1. Place-based heating and cooling
  2. Nature Based Solutions at city scale
  3. Urban energy systems
  4. City finance innovation for climate neutrality
  5. Large-scale building retrofits and renovations
  6. Decarbonising urban mobility and logistics

All applicants must:

  1. Choose the challenge area that resonates most and anchor the rationale for intervention within this area.
  2. Within their chosen challenge area, formulate an adequate context-specific impact pathway following the impact framework. While the impact pathway describes how the proposed intervention is expected to create change, the Impact Framework provides the progression from problem to impact and the structure for how that change will be monitored, evidenced and reported.


Across all challenge areas, ECT2 aims to enable cities to move from constrained implementation to durable, city-wide transformation by combining activities which remove diagnosed systemic blockers and accelerate progress to climate neutrality. To this end, the programme aims to ensure that Mission Cities can:

  1. Deploy and scale climate‑neutral solutions by addressing institutional, policy, financial, governance, market or social bottlenecks that limit uptake or speed.
  2. Translate research, innovation and evidence into operational policy and delivery systems, ensuring that scientific and technical knowledge is effectively embedded into city decision‑making.
  3. Strengthen city capacities and capabilities so that climate‑neutral delivery becomes business‑as‑usual, independent of individual champions or one‑off projects.
  4. Cover a broad range of levers for change (policy, green technology, finance, governance, behavioural change, social innovation, multi-actor collaboration, procurement, new business models as circular economy, etc.)
  5. Enable collaborative governance and citizen engagement models that support systemic, cross‑sectoral climate action and deliver just transition outcomes.


The selection of proposals will result in multiple implementation-enabling innovations focussing on resolving key implementation challenges. Interventions will work individually and in combinations/clusters to generate resolutions for shared barriers.


Activities eligible for funding are:

Interventions should consist of the following activities to be eligible for funding:

  1. Pioneering Activities: Activities that adapt, test or deploy innovative or enabling solutions at city level.
  2. Systemic, Science‑based Innovative Initiatives: Activities that strengthen the connection between research, evidence and city delivery.
  3. Capacity and capability‑building activities: Activities that establish new knowledge, skills and institutional competence within city administrations and key local actors.
  4. Collaborative governance and community‑building activities: Activities that build more collaborative, inclusive and systemic governance arrangements.


Please note: proposed interventions may cover several or all of these descriptions of eligible activities – this list is intended to allow for flexibility in proposing interventions, rather than limiting proposed interventions to any one eligible activity alone.

Applicants will be requested at the point of submitting a proposal to describe and declare the links between their proposed interventions and the eligible activities as listed above.

item.title: FuseNet Support of Master Students going on an internship abroad
item.description:
This support package is meant to facilitate MSc students in fusion who want to go abroad for an internship, thereby stimulating quality of education through exchanges. The internship can take place at a fusion research centre or university involved in fusion research. This place is not limited to Europe. Students registered at universities that are a FuseNet member and/or are doing their internship at hosts that are a FuseNet member, and their home university is located in one of the EUROfusion member states can apply for financial support for their internship here.

The financial support consists of a fixed amount of travel support (depending on the travel distance) and accommodation/living support (depending on the internship duration). The application has to be submitted at least 2 weeks before and within 6 months of the start of the internship. Other sources of funding for the internship (scholarships or grants, compensation or salary from the host institute, funds from other EU support schemes, etc.) need to be specified. Funding can also be restricted in cases where funding has been received from FuseNet in the past (see the terms and conditions on the FuseNet webpage).

item.title: FuseNet Support of Master Students in attending Educational Events
item.description:
This support scheme is launched to support and facilitate Master students to take part in educational activities external to their own organization. It allows Master students to participate in fusion Master classes, summer schools, and other short-term events with a dominant educational character. All conferences are excluded from support except when the Master student has his/her own contribution at the event (see terms and conditions for details).

Students registered at universities that are a FuseNet member and/or are seeking to attend educational activities at hosts that are a FuseNet member, and both the home university and the educational event are located in one of the countries that are part of the EUROfusion member states, can apply here for financial support to take part in a fusion-related educational training activity.

The financial support consists of a fixed amount of travel support (depending on the travel distance) and subsistence support (depending on the duration). The (training) activity has to take place at a university group or research institute in one of the EUROfusion members states or at a FuseNet member institute. The application has to be submitted at least 2 weeks before the actual start of the educational event. The educational event has to start no later than 6 months after application.

item.title: Phortify Internship (Traineeship) Grants - Pilot Call
item.description:
About Phortify

Phortify - Photonics Education Network for Next-Gen Innovation and Digital Skills Excellence for Industry and Society - is dedicated to the Enhancement and Harmonisation of Photonics education and training across Europe. Phortify offers a two-year European Master’s in Photonics Engineering, combining advanced coursework, hands-on laboratory training, and cutting-edge digital skills development, structured mobility windows and industry placements. Students who complete the Phortify track receive an official Phortify Certificate in addition to their Master’s degree. Students can enrol in a Phortify-related master programme at any of the 7 participating universities. In addition, Phortify provides stand-alone modules with harmonised standards for quality assurance and certification, offering high flexibility and mobility for both students and industry professionals. Finally, Phortify organises mentoring programmes for women postdocs and early PIs as well as one-day immersive experience events for prospective students, providing a unique opportunity to explore photonics and its applications.

About the Phortify Funding Framework

Phortify’s Funding Framework aims to widen participation in photonics by supporting students and staff who are traditionally underrepresented in STEM. This includes women and gender minorities, students from low-income or socio-economically disadvantaged backgrounds, first-generation university students, and learners with disabilities or specific support needs. The programme also encourages participation from regions with limited access to advanced higher education, as well as those belonging to cultural or minority groups that may be underrepresented in higher education. By addressing these dimensions of diversity, Phortify helps ensure a more inclusive and equitable community of future photonics professionals. Participants selected for Phortify funding receive financial support for studies and mobility pathways within the participating master programmes, or for mentoring programmes and STEM experience workshops organised by one of the Phortify partners.
